ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (as last amended, including Articles 2(1)(5), 4, and 5-2); Act on Prohibition of Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction (as last amended); Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information, Articles 10 and 10-2; Financial Services Commission Rules and Guidelines on Customer Due Diligence and Beneficial Owner Identification; and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, Article 6. UBO information is collected and held by regulated financial institutions and is accessible to the Financial Services Commission and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit under strict statutory gates; there is no publicly searchable UBO register in Korea.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Registered Corporate Matters Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry Office of the competent Korean District Court under the Supreme Court of Korea Court Administration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel Path A for Hague Apostille Convention States: notarize the Korean court-issued certificate at a Korean notary public, then obtain a single Hague Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; Parallel Path B for non-Apostille States: notarize the certificate at a Korean notary public, then obtain consular legalization from the embassy or consulate of the destination state accredited in Seoul. Use only one path, never chain Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Tax Clearance and Corporate Registration Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean National Tax Service and Registry Office of the competent District Court
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel Path A: Korean notarization plus Hague Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for member states of the Apostille Convention; Parallel Path B: Korean notarization plus consular legalization by the destination state embassy or consulate in Korea for non-member states. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution Approving Incorporation, Appointment of Officers, and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Chusik Hoesa, with Korean notarial authentication of corporate signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel Path A: notarize all signatures at a Korean notary public and then obtain one Hague Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs; Parallel Path B: notarize at a Korean notary public and then process consular legalization at the destination state embassy or consulate in Seoul. Select only the path required by the receiving jurisdiction; do not apply Apostille and consular legalization to the same document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Chusik Hoesa Articles of Incorporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators and initial shareholders, with mandatory Korean notarial formality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel Path A: notarize the Articles in Korea, then apply for a single Hague Apostille with the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille Convention jurisdictions; Parallel Path B: notarize the Articles in Korea, then submit to the destination state embassy or consulate in Korea for consular legalization for non-Apostille jurisdictions. These pathways are parallel and mutually exclusive; no sequential combination is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a Korean Licensed Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank in Korea supervised by the Financial Services Commission
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel Path A: after bank officer countersignature, notarize the letter at a Korean notary public and obtain a Hague Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for use in Apostille states; Parallel Path B: after notarization in Korea, obtain consular legalization at the destination state embassy or consulate in Seoul for use in non-Apostille states. Use only the applicable path; never layer Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Declaration and AML/CFT Due Diligence Questionnaire
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company secretarial or AML compliance counsel retained by the Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel Path A: notarize the declaration by the beneficial owners in Korea and apply for a single Hague Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille states; Parallel Path B: notarize the declaration in Korea and obtain consular legalization from the destination state embassy or consulate in Korea for non-Apostille states. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must be selected based on the destination jurisdiction alone.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before any filing, counsel must screen all shareholders, directors, officers, authorized signatories, ultimate beneficial owners, and counterparties against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions designations, Interpol and domestic criminal repositories, and vendor negative-news databases. Every natural person holding at least 25 percent must be treated as a beneficial owner; lower thresholds apply for PEPs, court officials, military officers, and persons connected to sanctions evasion in anti-dumping trade-remedy matters. PEP screening must cover immediate family members and close associates, with enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval for any adverse hit. Screening must be repeated each time the control structure changes and continuously during the first year of operation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS) - Online Corporate Name Search and Registration Filing System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory trade name of a Chusik Hoesa must be stated in Korean Hangul and must include the liability-form suffix Chusik Hoesa. Foreign words are transliterated phonetically into Hangul; a separate English or romanized name may be used in parentheses but cannot replace the Hangul statutory name. The four-tier naming convention applies: Tier 1 distinctive element identifying the undertaking; Tier 2 business description related to anti-dumping trade defense and customs consulting; Tier 3 mandatory suffix Chusik Hoesa; and Tier 4 optional geographic or structural marker. The name must not be identical or deceptively similar to a registered trade name in the same or related business and must not contain words that mislead the public about licensing or public authority.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If IROS rejects the proposed name, the applicant must request written grounds from the registry office. Within 14 days, the applicant or Korean counsel must file a written reconsideration with the same District Court registration office, attaching a corrected Hangul name, proof that no identical or confusingly similar name is registered, and, if a sensitive token was included, a ministerial approval from the competent authority. If the registration office maintains the rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal to the competent administrative court under the Administrative Litigation Act within 90 days of service of the final rejection. No extension of a name reservation is allowed after the 30-day window; the applicant must resubmit a new name-search application and pay the applicable official fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable as the sole registered address for this anti-dumping trade defense consulting Chusik Hoesa. The Korean National Tax Service Hometax registration regime requires the registered place of business to be a physical location where tax records, books, and officers are available. Korean commercial banks uniformly reject virtual office addresses when opening corporate accounts for cross-border service companies, requiring an executed lease, utility bill, signboard photograph, and physical substance. For a licensed trade-remedy defense practice, a professional office with controlled file access, meeting rooms, and personnel is expected; a mere virtual address would trigger tax disallowances, bank account refusal, and AML enhanced scrutiny.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspection: registered signboard displayed at street level; original lease agreement with the actual owner; utility bills in the entity name; physical attendance of at least one director or designated officer; availability of corporate books and tax records; functioning telephone and correspondence handling; and evidence that anti-dumping consulting files are stored on site or in a verifiable secure system. Quantified risk: 15 percent base annual probability of inspection for a low-risk professional services company; 80 percent escalation if a virtual office or mail drop is used; 45 percent escalation if the entity is foreign controlled and has no staff on site; risk drops to 5 percent when the physical office, lease, and staff are fully compliant.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), particularly Articles 288 (Articles of Incorporation), 289 (Execution of Incorporation), 290 (Minimum Capital), 291 (Declaration of Contributions), 292 (Promoters' Subscription), 295 (Payment of Contributions), 296 (Inspection of Contribution Performance), 297 (Meeting of Incorporation), 302 (Application for Incorporation Registration), 312 (Registration of Incorporation), 317 (Registration Deadline), 330 (Post-Incorporation Matters: Appointment of Directors and Statutory Auditors), 340 (Legal Representative Authority), and 542 (Public Notice and Electronic Disclosure under the External Audit and Supervision Act); supplementary provisions of the Enforcement Decree of the Commercial Act regarding registration forms and filing fees.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division, Seoul District Court (Seoul Central District Court Registration Office), or the district court registry (Deung-gi-so) having territorial jurisdiction over the registered head office address; online filings through the Supreme Court Electronic Registration System (I-reg / 인터넷등기소) with final paper filing at the designated court registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan) together with the Certificate of Share Subscription (Jung-bu), Payment Certificate (Nabip-gwanri-jeung), Minutes of the Incorporation Meeting, and the Registration of Incorporation Application (Seollip-deung-gi-sincheongseo) filed with the registry under Article 302 of the Commercial Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None: For a Chusik Hoesa formed for ISIC 7490 trade-defense consulting, Korean law now imposes no statutory minimum capital under the amended Commercial Act (Act No. 15977 of 2017), provided the company is not a financial services or designated licensed entity; however, the founders must still pay at least 100 Korean won per share (par value), fully paid in at incorporation, and amounts received must be credited to a blocked capital subscription account (or in-kind contribution assessment) before registration. The escrow/blocked account rule under Article 295(1) requires the full subscription price to be paid into a bank branch in Korea designated by the incorporator, and the account must remain frozen until the incorporation registration is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME], A CHUSIK HOESA INCORPORATED UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA, ADOPTED IN WRITING WITHOUT A BOARD MEETING PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 391-2 OF THE COMMERCIAL ACT (OR AT A DULY CONVENED MEETING HELD ON THIS __ DAY OF ________, 20__, AT THE REGISTERED OFFICE OF THE COMPANY). THE FOLLOWING DIRECTORS WERE PRESENT OR CONSENTED IN WRITING: [DIRECTOR A], [DIRECTOR B], AND [DIRECTOR C], WITH ALL DIRECTORS OF THE COMPANY BEING PRESENT OR HAVING SIGNED A WRITTEN CONSENT, AND THE MEETING HAVING SATISFIED THE QUORUM REQUIREMENTS OF ARTICLE 393 AND ARTICLE 371 OF THE COMMERCIAL ACT. HAVING CONSIDERED AND DELIBERATED UPON THE INCORPORATION OF THE COMPANY, THE SUBSCRIPTION AND PAYMENT OF SHARE CAPITAL, THE ESTABLISHMENT OF THE REGISTERED OFFICE, THE APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS, AND THE BANKING ARRANGEMENTS REQUIRED FOR THE COMMENCEMENT OF THE COMPANY'S BUSINESS, THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS HEREBY ADOPTS THE FOLLOWING RESOLUTIONS: FIRST, THE BOARD CONFIRMS THAT THE COMPANY WAS DULY INCORPORATED BY REGISTRATION WITH THE KOREA LEGAL REGISTRY ON [DATE OF REGISTRATION], AND THAT THE ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION AS REGISTERED, INCLUDING THE CORPORATE PURPOSE OF PROVISION OF LEGAL, ACCOUNTING, AND TRADE-REMEDY CONSULTING SERVICES RELATING TO INTERNATIONAL ANTI-DUMPING INVESTIGATIONS, SHALL CONSTITUTE THE SUPREME GOVERNING INSTRUMENT OF THE COMPANY. SECOND, THE BOARD CONFIRMS THAT THE TOTAL AUTHORIZED SHARE CAPITAL OF THE COMPANY IS [AUTHORIZED CAPITAL IN KRW] SPLIT INTO [NUMBER] SHARES OF PAR VALUE [PAR VALUE IN KRW] EACH, AND THAT THE ISSUED AND OUTSTANDING SHARE CAPITAL IS [ISSUED CAPITAL IN KRW] FULLY PAID IN THE COMPANY'S CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION ACCOUNT AT [BANK NAME] IN THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA. THE BOARD RESOLVES THAT THE PAID-IN CAPITAL BE OBSERVED AS UNRESTRICTED FOR USE IN THE COMPANY'S BUSINESS ACTIVITIES, SUBJECT TO THE COMPANY'S CASH-MANAGEMENT POLICIES AND APPLICABLE LAW. THIRD, THE BOARD RESOLVES THAT THE REGISTERED OFFICE OF THE COMPANY SHALL BE [FULL ADDRESS IN THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA] (WHICH IS IDENTICAL TO THE ADDRESS IN THE CERTIFICATE OF REGISTRATION AND THE ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION), AND THE BOARD AUTHORIZES THE CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER AND/OR THE REPRESENTATIVE DIRECTOR TO ENTER INTO AND TERMINATE LEASES, TO EXTEND OR RENEW SUCH LEASES, AND TO FILE ANY CHANGE-OF-REGISTERED-OFFICE NOTICES WITH THE APPROPRIATE DISTRICT COURT REGISTRY IN ACCORDANCE WITH ARTICLE 317 OF THE COMMERCIAL ACT. FOURTH, THE BOARD APPOINTS THE FOLLOWING STATUTORY OFFICERS OF THE COMPANY: REPRESENTATIVE DIRECTOR [NAME] (WHO SHALL ALSO SERVE AS CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER), DIRECTORS [NAMES], AND STATUTORY AUDITOR (Gam-sa) [NAME] IF THE COMPANY MEETS, OR OPTIONALLY APPOINTS AN AUDITOR COMMITTEE IF SO REQUIRED BY LAW OR THE ARTICLES; SUBJECT TO THE REQUIREMENT THAT ANY STATUTORY AUDITOR SHALL NOT SIMULTANEOUSLY SERVE AS A DIRECTOR, EXECUTIVE, OR EMPLOYEE OF THE COMPANY, IN ACCORDANCE WITH ARTICLE 411 OF THE COMMERCIAL ACT. FIFTH, THE BOARD RESOLVES THAT THE FOLLOWING OFFICERS SHALL HAVE SOLE OR JOINT SIGNATURE RIGHTS AS LEGAL REPRESENTATIVES OF THE COMPANY FOR ALL PURPOSES UNDER KOREAN LAW: THE REPRESENTATIVE DIRECTOR, AND, JOINTLY, ANY TWO OF THE DIRECTORS LISTED IN THE ANNUAL COMMERCIAL REGISTER, ACTING IN THE MANNER SPECIFIED IN THE COMPANY'S ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION AND NOTIFICATIONS PROVIDED TO THE REGISTRY. SIXTH, THE BOARD RESOLVES THAT THE COMPANY SHALL MAINTAIN ONE OR MORE CORPORATE BANK ACCOUNTS WITH COMMERCIAL BANKS IN THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA, AND THE BOARD HEREBY AUTHORIZES THE REPRESENTATIVE DIRECTOR AND THE OFFICERS NAMED ABOVE, EITHER JOINTLY OR INDIVIDUALLY AS DETERMINED BY THE BOARD, TO OPEN SUCH ACCOUNTS, TO DEPOSIT AND WITHDRAW FUNDS, TO ISSUE CHECKS AND ELECTRONIC FUND TRANSFERS, TO CONFIRM SWIFT/WIRE TRANSFER RECEIPTS IN US DOLLARS AND KOREAN WON, AND TO EXECUTE ALL BANKING INSTRUCTIONS, LOAN DOCUMENTS, E-SIGNATURES, AND DIGITAL-CERTIFICATE APPLICATIONS IN THE COMPANY'S NAME. SEVENTH, THE BOARD VESTS IN THE REPRESENTATIVE DIRECTOR AND THE FINANCE DIRECTOR (OR THEIR DESIGNATED DELEGATE) THE POWER TO APPOINT REASONABLE OUTSIDE COUNSEL, LAW FIRMS, OR CERTIFIED PUBLIC ACCOUNTANTS FOR THE COMPANY'S INTERNATIONAL TRADE-DEFENSE CONSULTING ACTIVITIES, AND TO EXECUTE ENGAGEMENT AGREEMENTS AND SERVICE CONTRACTS REQUIRED FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF CLIENT REPRESENTATION BEFORE GOVERNMENTAL AND QUASI-GOVERNMENTAL TRADE-REMEDY AUTHORITIES WITHIN AND OUTSIDE THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA. EIGHTH, THE BOARD RESOLVES THAT THE COMPANY SHALL IMMEDIATELY OBTAIN ALL REGISTRATIONS, PERMITS, AND LICENSES THAT ARE REQUIRED FOR ITS CONSULTING ACTIVITIES UNDER RELEVANT KOREAN LAWS INCLUDING THE LICENSE FOR FOREIGN TRADE AND THE KOREA TRADE INVESTMENT PROMOTION AGENCY ('KOTRA') REGISTRATION WHERE APPLICABLE, AND THE BOARD DIRECTS MANAGEMENT TO IMPLEMENT A COMPLIANCE MANUAL COVERING THE LEGAL ETHICS AND PROFESSIONAL RESPONSIBILITY REQUIREMENTS FOR RENDERING TRADE-REMEDY CONSULTING SERVICES. NINTH, THE BOARD RESOLVES THAT THE COMPANY'S FISCAL YEAR SHALL COMMENCE ON JANUARY 1 AND END ON DECEMBER 31 OF EACH YEAR, AND THAT THE FIRST FISCAL YEAR SHALL COMMENCE ON THE DATE OF INCORPORATION REGISTRATION AND END ON DECEMBER 31 OF THAT YEAR. ALL ACTIONS EMPLOYED TO IMPLEMENT THIS RESOLUTION AND THE AGENCY OF ANY BANK, REGISTRY OFFICIAL, OR COUNSEL FOR THE COMPANY ARE HEREBY RATIFIED, CONFIRMED, AND ADOPTED AS THE ACTIONS OF THE COMPANY. THIS RESOLUTION IS EFFECTIVE AS OF ITS ADOPTION AND SHALL REMAIN IN FULL FORCE AND EFFECT UNTIL REVOKED OR AMENDED BY A DULY ADOPTED BOARD RESOLUTION. DATED THIS ___ DAY OF ______________, 20___ IN [CITY], REPUBLIC OF KOREA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of Company Name and Verification of Business Scope under Foreign Trade and Trade Remedies Laws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Seoul District Court Registry / Korean Supreme Court e-Registry (인터넷등기소), and, for export/trade-remedy aspects, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) and Korea Trade Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) guidance desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a prior name search on the Supreme Court e-Registry to ensure that the proposed Korean name of the Chusik Hoesa is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company in the same or similar business line. Prepare an executory draft of the Articles of Incorporation in the Korean language including the corporate purpose covering professional consulting services for anti-dumping, countervailing duty, and trade-defense investigations; expressly state the intended use of the Seoul or local jurisdiction. Confirm that the business scope (ISIC 7490, NAICS 541199 equivalent) is classified as non-regulated professional consulting not requiring a separate statutory operational permit before formation. Download the officially prescribed application forms from the I-reg portal, verify the jurisdiction of the intended registered office, and ensure that the registered address is a physical, accessible location for service of process and registry correspondence. Where the founding directors include foreign residents, verify passport notarization requirements and arrange for apostilled or consular-authenticated identification documents translated into Korean by a certified translator.
required_dossiers: Certificate of name-search confirmation (or a non-conflicting name registration receipt) from the Supreme Court e-Registry
Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean (Jeong-gwan)
Identification documents of all promoters/directors (resident registration cards or passport copies)
If foreign promoter: apostilled/consular-legalized passport and certified Korean translation
Power of attorney in Korean for local agent if promoter is non-resident
Address proof of the proposed registered office (building register extract, lease agreement or written consent of the property owner)
Brief scope-of-business description in Korean for the non-banking AML risk profile
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to identical or confusingly similar existing registration, immediately prepare a secondary name choice, re-run the search, and refile electronically within 1 Business Day. If the proposed business scope is adjudged too broad or impermissible for a trade-defense consulting entity, narrow the purpose clause to 'legal and accounting support services, customs and trade-consulting, government relations, research and translation services' and re-submit with an explanatory cover memo. In cases of portal authentication failure, contact the e-Registry help desk or appoint an administrative agent (beon-ho-sa) to correct the digital certificate issues.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription Payment into Blocked Capital Collection Account and Preparation of Subscription Audit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in the Republic of Korea (e.g., Kookmin Bank, Shinhan Bank, Hana Bank, or Woori Bank) and the incorporators' designated bank branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate creation deposit account in the name of the company being formed (or in the promoter's name) and deposit the full subscription price for the total issued shares, with the proviso that the account is blocked/frozen until incorporation registration is completed. Under Article 295(1) of the Commercial Act, require the bank to issue a certificate of subscription payment or deposit receipt (nabip-gwanri jeungmyeong-seo) clearly indicating the subscriber's name, the amount paid, the date, and the account number, and indicating that the funds are restricted from withdrawal. Ensure that the paid amount is in Korean won and that any foreign-currency Swift/USD subscription and treasury transactions, as intended for future consulting fee receipts, are settled into a separate operating account after registration; do not intermingle prior to registration. If the subscription price is to be paid in kind (e.g., contributed software, copyrights, or intangibles for trade-defense advisory tools), appoint a court-approved appraiser and prepare an in-kind property report. Retain bank fee receipts and obtain a computer-readable copy of the payment certificate for submission to the registry via the I-reg system.
required_dossiers: Passbook/bank statement of the blocked capital account
Capital subscription payment certificate issued by the bank (Article 295 certificate)
Resolution of promoters confirming subscription terms
In-kind property valuation report, if applicable
Written consent of each subscriber to allocate shares
Wire transfer or cash payment receipts
Subscriber list (ju-mo-yeong-nak-jang)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues a defective certificate or omits the blocked-account wording, re-apply to the bank's branch manager and request a corrected payment certificate under the standard Commercial Act form; if the bank refuses because the account name differs from the final corporate name, amend the account description to 'company name pending incorporation' and ask for an explanatory letter. If a subscriber fails to pay, modify the subscription list by withdrawal of the defaulting subscriber and re-notarization, then update the subscription count and re-run the payment certificate process. In the event of the bank's refusal to freeze the account, select another major commercial bank branch that offers statutory incorporation deposit services.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Convocation of the Incorporation General Meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public (Beop-mu-sa or Gongjeong-in) within the jurisdiction of the proposed head office, or the registrar office's notarial window; thereafter the Incorporation Meeting in accordance with Articles 297–302 of the Commercial Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Korean notary to authenticate the Articles of Incorporation signed by all incorporators, and pay the notarial fee based on paid-in capital. Prepare for submission to the notary the final certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation, the list of incorporators, the completed subscription payment certificate, and the minutes of the meeting of incorporators to be held immediately after notarization. At the incorporation meeting, obtain unanimous consent or a majority vote of subscriber votes with a presence quorum; specifically pass the following agenda items: (i) confirmation of contribution performance, (ii) election of directors and a statutory auditor, (iii) appointment of a representative director. Ensure that directors elected are not under disqualification under Articles 398 (prohibition of fraudulent means), 542 (audit committee rules), and 466 (self-dealing restrictions). Draw up the official minutes, obtain signatures or seals of subscribers, and attach the election acceptance certificates of each director and auditor. The notarized Articles must reflect the exact capital, head office address in Korea, corporate name, purpose, and standard provisions on issue of shares, transfer restrictions, and board authority required by the registry.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (three original copies with notary seal)
Minutes of the incorporation meeting or written consent resolutions (hojeong)
Certificate of subscription payment from the bank
Subscriber list
Certificate of election and written acceptance of each director and auditor
Report on in-kind contribution if applicable
Statutory inspection report on contribution performance, if any
Legal representative's identification and registered seal certificate (in-doin-jang-jeung-myeong-seo)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a defect in the draft articles (e.g., missing clause on transfer restrictions, improper corporate purpose), amend the draft by supplemental resolution of the incorporators, re-notarize the entire Articles, and reperform any necessary signatures. If the incorporation meeting is invalidly convened due to short notice or improper waiver, re-notify all incorporators and hold a fresh meeting. If an elected director withdraws consent, hold a supplemental election by written resolution and file supplemental minutes before registration. If the notary requires a Korean translation of foreign-language passport, obtain a certified Korean translation and present it with the original.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Incorporation Registration and Issuance of Certificate of Corporate Seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Seoul Central District Court Registration Office (or the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered head office), via the internet registry (I-reg) then in-person submission or postal submission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for registration of incorporation (Seollip-deung-gi) within any lawful timeframe but promptly after satisfying all incorporations matters. The application must be submitted within one month from the date of payment of contributions pursuant to Article 317(1) of the Commercial Act, together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, minutes, payment certificate, and director/auditor acceptance documents. Pay the registration fee (registration duty tax and local education tax) based on paid-in capital, which for a no-minimum-capital consulting company generally ranges from KRW 6,000 to KRW 30,000 for capital below KRW 100 million, plus a court revenue stamp. Upon submission, the registrar verifies statutory compliance, then posts the registration entry to the commercial register; after registration, apply for the corporate seal registration in the same registry or via the notary to obtain the corporate seal certificate (in-doin-jang-jeung-myeong-seo). Also open the corporate seal account at the bank and update the company's official address. Receive the certified extract of the commercial register (deung-gi-sa-jeung) and corporate registration certificate, which serve as primary legal existence evidence for banks, KOTRA, and government authorities.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of incorporation (prescribed form)
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Minutes of incorporation meeting
Certificate of subscription payment
List of directors, statutory auditor, and representative director, with written acceptances
Certificate of registered seal of the representative director
Power of attorney if filing through an agent
Receipt for payment of registration fee and local education tax
Copy of the head office lease contract or consent document
Foreigner legalization documents, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry notifies a deficiency or 'request for supplementation,' cure the defect within 2 weeks by filing a supplementary document; common deficiencies include unaligned seal impression, missing payment certificate, or mismatch of corporate purpose. If an error in the registered head office address is detected, file a motion for correction of the register. If registration exceeds the statutory period, the incorporation can be voidable or promoters may be civilly liable; if the registry refuses registration, request a written rejection notice and re-apply after rectification, and consider a petition to the court for an order compelling registration if the refusal is arbitrary.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of SMEs and Startups (MSS) and the Korea Federation of Small and Medium Business (K-biz) as administrative coordinator; primary regulatory authority for trade-defense consulting services is the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the Trade Commission (KTC) and the Korea Trade Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) for trade-remedy-related advisory registration; professional service conduct is monitored by the Korean Bar Association or the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants only where licensed professionals are engaged.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not a manufacturing license; applicable title is the 'General Industrial Consulting and Trade Remedy Service Business Registration' under the Foreign Trade Act, together with a professional legal/accounting accreditation for lawyers or CPAs employed in the practice; if the company provides legal advocacy in anti-dumping proceedings, it must either employ Korean-licensed attorneys or contract as a sub-consultant to a licensed foreign law firm, and register as a 'foreign trading agent' or 'trade-support institution' with customs/trade authorities where applicable

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea (with delegated enforcement by the Korea Environment Corporation) and the respective Si/Gun/Gu environmental authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable for pure consultancy operations under ISIC 7490; no physical project with land area, industrial discharge or emission source exists. If the trade-defense office includes a non-metallic, non-industrial data center with no stationary combustion sources, only a 'small-scale environmental registration' may apply if the floor area exceeds thresholds; otherwise file a voluntary Environmental Impact Assessment scoping opinion only at the building owner's request
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable: The consulting activity does not generate process wastewater, volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions, or hazardous waste. For baseline administrative compliance, the office must observe the Clean Air Conservation Act for any incidental VOCs from printing operations, keeping total annual VOC emissions below the fugitive-source threshold generally corresponding to 0.1 tons per year or an air pollutant facility threshold in Article 2 of the Clean Air Conservation Act and the Enforcement Decree; waste disposal must follow the Wastes Control Act for general office waste, and any electronic-waste recycling must be consigned to a licensed recycler
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and life-safety certification of the registered office under the Fire Prevention, Fire Fighting, Rescue and Medical Service Act: obtain a 'Fire-fighting System Certificate of Completion' from the Korea Fire Institute or the local fire station if the office building is new/renovated, and ensure the building's fire inspection is current under the 'Fire Safety Management Regulation' for business premises. For a pure consulting office, civil defense clearance (min-bang) is generally not required; however, the workplace must have a fire extinguisher per 100m², evacuation signs, and be included in the building's annual fire safety training program. Where employees are hired, a 'Machinery, Electric and Construction Equipment Safety Inspection' is not required, but the company must file an occupational safety and health initiation notice with the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA) if the workplace is not exempt under Article 3 of the Occupational Safety and Health Act; if the company has more than one employee, it must secure workers' compensation insurance through the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service and file the initial report on business commencement.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, with electronic filing through Hometax (www.hometax.go.kr); Korea Customs Service (KCS) for customs and export declaration processing via UNI-PASS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity beginning taxable activities in Korea: (1) appoint a statutory tax representative in Korea; (2) prepare the Korean Business Registration Application prescribed under the Value-Added Tax Act, together with the foreign corporate charter/registration certificate, articles of incorporation, proof of local place of business or tax representative address, and a notarized power of attorney; (3) file the application with the district tax office of the NTS having jurisdiction over the local business place or the tax representative's address; (4) upon approval, obtain the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which functions as the TIN and VAT registration number, and the Korean Business Registration Certificate (Saupja Deungrokjeung). Where a non-resident entity has no domestic establishment but makes Korean taxable supplies or receives VAT refundable consideration, VAT registration is completed through the tax representative at the competent NTS office; absence of registration does not extinguish the statutory VAT liability.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. A Korean Chusik Hoesa is automatically an entity-level corporate income taxpayer under the Corporate Income Tax Act; Korea does not offer check-the-box or pass-through elections, and no hybrid mismatch entity election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT registration exemption threshold exists in Korea; every business operator must register with the district tax office. The KRW 80,000,000 threshold applies only to simplified taxable individual taxpayers, not to a Chusik Hoesa, which is always a general taxable person.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory NTS e-Tax Invoice system for business-to-business supplies, using Hometax or the NTS Open API; e-tax invoices must be transmitted to the NTS by the day following the supply date. For business-to-consumer cash transactions exceeding KRW 10,000, a cash receipt must be issued and transmitted to the NTS. The system relies on approved invoice identification numbers and centralized data matching rather than a real-time fiscal stamping regime; failure to transmit or late transmission triggers additional tax penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and certain exported services are zero-rated under the Value-Added Tax Act. For goods, title and physical movement must pass from Korea to a foreign destination, evidenced by an accepted export declaration. For services such as anti-dumping trade defense consulting, zero rating applies when the service is supplied to a non-resident for use or benefit outside Korea and the consideration is received in foreign currency from a foreign source; the service must not be effectively consumed in Korea.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (processed and accepted on the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS System)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate (Foreign Exchange Bank purchase/sale record showing foreign currency receipts)
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent proof of privileged foreign exchange receipt
Service contract and evidence of overseas performance and foreign use/benefit for zero-rated consulting services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service cross-check export declarations, e-tax invoices, transport records, and bank foreign-exchange settlements. If a zero-rated export cannot be substantiated, the supply is reclassified as taxable, resulting in VAT assessed at 10%, interest, and late-payment penalties. For fraudulent or grossly negligent claims, additional tax of up to 40% of the understated VAT may be imposed, along with reversal of claimed input VAT. Criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act is possible for fabricated export documentation or fictitious foreign-exchange settlement.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.refund_substantiation_note: For services zero-rating, the taxpayer must retain both the foreign-exchange receipt evidence and the underlying commercial contract to demonstrate that the consideration was repatriated to Korea within the statutory 180-day period and that the service was performed outside Korea.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (The Bank of Korea, under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, with Ministry of Economy and Finance policy authority)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a largely free-floating managed currency regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA) and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations. The Bank of Korea acts as the central bank responsible for exchange-rate policy, foreign reserves management, and FX transaction monitoring, while the Ministry of Economy and Finance retains delegated authority for capital-transaction licensing and reporting. Korean won convertibility is liberalized for current-account transactions; foreign-currency receipts such as export proceeds may be credited into foreign-currency accounts of domestic foreign-exchange banks without mandatory forced conversion, though incoming remittances require bank reporting through the Foreign Exchange Information System. For capital-account transactions, including equity investment in a Chusik Hoesa, cross-border remittances are generally permitted if reportable, but the investor or entity must file a foreign-exchange declaration through a designated foreign-exchange bank before or within a prescribed grace period. Dividends and profit remittances are subject to withholding tax under Korean tax law and cross-border tax treaties; banks will require tax payment certificates, certified financial statements, and proof of no unresolved regulatory issues. The key practical hurdle is not formal inconvertibility but documentary strictness: banks demand real-name identification, purpose-code accuracy, and a contamination-free capital path before releasing foreign currency into won.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be received in foreign currency and credited to a domestic foreign-exchange bank account, either kept in foreign currency or converted into Korean won, within the statutory export collection period of six months from the date of shipment or export declaration. The exporter must file receipt evidence through the Foreign Exchange Information System, and although there is no mandated percentage of hard surrender, the full remittance must be returned into the Korean banking system. Extensions require approval from the Korea Trade Insurance Corporation or the relevant foreign-exchange bank under exceptional documentary evidence.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Korean Won Corporate Settlement Account and Foreign Currency Demand Deposit Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Capital Escrow Account
Korean Won Current Account and Multi-Currency Foreign Exchange Account
Capital Escrow Account and USD/KRW Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to medium as a primary account. Foreign fintech EMIs without a Korean Electronic Financial Business license cannot hold Korean won current accounts, cannot execute Korean foreign-exchange purpose-code reporting, and are not acceptable for statutory capital verification or export-proceeds admission. Wise, Airwallex, and Payoneer may operate only as ancillary collection rails for certain approved service fees, but they are not legally equivalent to a tier-1 Korean foreign-exchange bank. For an anti-dumping trade-defense consulting entity, a licensed domestic bank account is mandatory and unlicensed foreign EMIs should not be proposed for capital subscriptions, foreign-currency clearing, or any transaction that requires Korean legal evidence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: South Korean foreign-exchange banks normally require at least one statutory director, especially a foreign director, to appear physically in-branch for initial corporate account opening to sign banking agreements and complete the real-name identification process. Remote consular proxy opening is not a universal right; some tier-1 banks may accept an apostilled notarized power of attorney verified by a Korean consulate or a Korean-certified notary, followed by a live video interview of the statutory director. In all cases, the bank will insist on a domestic Korea nexus through a registered office, a resident manager, or a service provider before issuing account credentials.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner is a non-resident foreign national with no Korean address or tax identity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled and notarized passports of all natural persons holding more than 25%, certified beneficial-ownership declaration, Korean tax identification number or foreign tax residence certificate, six-month source-of-wealth bank statements, certified criminal record certificates, and a signed declaration of the direct investor relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between the declared anti-dumping legal-defense consulting business and the expected cross-border payments profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal engagement letters from anti-dumping counsel, non-conflicting trade-remedy case dockets involving Korean exporter clients, itemized fee schedules, professional licenses of the legal and accounting principals, the target entity business plan, and a forecast of counterparties and purpose codes for all proposed wire flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party remittance or capital injection originating from a shell entity rather than the named equity investor
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete corporate ownership map ending in the remitting bank, certified board resolution of the Chusik Hoesa authorizing the share subscription, the subscription agreement, SWIFT MT103 references of the investor bank, apostilled certificate of incorporation of the remitter, and a no-third-party settlement undertaking.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived use of the consulting account to bypass Korean foreign-exchange reporting on trade-related funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A treasury protocol showing separate accounts for capital injection, operating fees, and anti-dumping cost reimbursements, pre-approved FX purpose-code mapping, tax clearance certificates for each outbound disbursement, and monthly foreign-exchange reporting files to the Foreign Exchange Information System.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The share subscription in Korean won or foreign currency must be remitted from the foreign investor's own regulated bank account by SWIFT MT103 or an equivalent wire transfer, using a direct-investment transaction purpose code for external equity contribution under the Foreign Exchange Information System. The receiving Korean foreign-exchange bank requires a copy of the Chusik Hoesa board resolution, the share subscription agreement, the remitter's bank KYC certificate, and proof of transaction reporting. After the remittance is credited, the entity's certified public accountant issues a capital verification certificate only upon actual paid-in capital; public offering proceeds for anti-dumping defense fees must not be commingled.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The entity may pay overseas anti-dumping counsel, economic experts, auditors, and testing laboratories by SWIFT MT103 using a services or trade-related consulting purpose code. Korean banks require the underlying service contract, invoice, mileage of fees, and transaction-specific tax clearance before outward remittance. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are better suited to physical goods trade with shipping and insurance documents; for intellectual property and trade-defense advisory services, MT103 wire transfer is the dominant clearing rail. Disbursements must remain within the bank-approved account purpose and be supported by a documented commercial or legal obligation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore Korean Won Forward Contract with a designated foreign-exchange bank, strictly limited to documented current-account or trade-related underlying exposure and prohibited for speculative positions.

Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) for KRW is permissible when the underlying trade or investment transaction is verified and the bank files all required foreign-exchange reports; naked NDF positions are not permitted for this entity.

Cross-Currency Swap (KRW versus USD) aligned to known scheduled remittances, capital repayment, or profit distribution is permissible as a hedge only when cash-flow maturity and notional amounts are evidenced.
The entity may not use exotic FX options or structured derivatives; only vanilla hedging instruments with clear trade documentation are compliant with South Korean foreign-exchange regulations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Convening and holding the Ordinary General Meeting of Shareholders and approving the annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: None (internal corporate body); auditor's statement separately filed with the Financial Services Commission where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the meeting by the deadline exposes directors to an administrative fine under the Commercial Act (Article 635, not exceeding approximately KRW 5 million); any shareholder or statutory auditor may petition the court to order the meeting; persistent non-compliance can lead to removal of directors and, upon creditor application, compulsory dissolution and strike-off from the court register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and settlement of corporation tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the competent regional tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the end of the 3rd month after the fiscal year end; for a December 31 fiscal year, March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: additional tax of 20% of the unpaid tax (40% for fraudulent non-filing); underreporting: 10% additional tax; late payment interest of 0.022% per day accrues from the statutory due date until full payment; continuous delinquency permits tax seizure, auction of assets, revocation of business registration by the NTS and a creditor/court compulsory dissolution application resulting in administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax return and local income tax payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government (Si/Gun/Gu) through the local tax authority of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the national corporate income tax filing deadline; for a December 31 fiscal year, no later than April 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or underpayment subjects the company to additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid local income tax and daily late-payment interest at 0.022% from the due date; prolonged non-payment can lead to local government petition for compulsory dissolution and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit report and audited financial statements submitted to the Financial Supervisory Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) / Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For mandatory audit targets, the auditor must deliver its report to the company within 2 weeks of completion; the company must file it with the FSS within 2 weeks of receipt and in any case concurrently with the ordinary general meeting (within 3 months of fiscal year end for a calendar-year company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-submission of the auditor's report attracts a negligence fine under Article 15 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (up to KRW 20 million); the FSC may compel amendment of financial statements; for listed entities, delayed filing can trigger KRX trading halts and delisting; if an adverse audit opinion is not remedied, shareholders/creditors may obtain a court dissolution order culminating in strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Change Report (annual UBO/shareholding event confirmation for foreign-invested Chusik Hoesa)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) on behalf of the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days from the date of any share transfer, capital change, change of foreign investor identity/nationality, change of voting ratio, or amendment of the articles of association affecting foreign investment; an annual confirmation is required only if a reportable event occurred in the preceding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to notify within the 30-day window triggers an administrative fine for negligence under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (up to KRW 3 million), loss of tax benefits attached to foreign-invested enterprise status, and possible cancellation of foreign investment registration; combined tax and local delinquencies will accelerate court dissolution and removal from the corporate register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Chusik Hoesa becomes a mandatory external audit target if it satisfies any of the following quantitative tests under Article 2 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies: (1) total assets in the immediately preceding fiscal year are KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9 million) or more at year-end; (2) it is a stock corporation listed or admitted on the Korea Exchange (KRX); (3) total assets at year-end are KRW 7 billion (approximately USD 5.2 million) or more and annual total revenue is KRW 70 billion (approximately USD 52 million) or more; (4) total assets at year-end are KRW 7 billion or more and average full-time employees are 300 or more; or (5) the Securities and Futures Commission designates the company as audit-required because it is a financial company, public-interest company, or a company needing investor protection. The thresholds apply based on the immediately preceding fiscal year and are consolidated for parent companies with subsidiaries.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) as adopted by the Korean Accounting Standards Board; listed companies and all external audit targets must apply K-IFRS, while non-listed non-mandatory small companies may prepare accounts under K-GAAP (Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, including SME standards). Audit procedures follow Korean Standards on Auditing (KSA), which align with International Standards on Auditing (ISA).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea's legal framework does not impose an annual neutral UBO form-filing for ordinary Chusik Hoesa companies; the operative statutory mechanism is the 30-day event-based report to KOTRA/MOTIE under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, plus shareholder register updates under the Commercial Act. Any foreign investment transfer, capital increase/decrease, change of foreign investor name/nationality, change in share ratio, or relocation of the registered office must be reported within 30 days; shareholder register entries must be updated on request and at least at each AGM record date. The external auditor must obtain and verify the ultimate beneficial ownership breakdown from management and include it in audit working papers. Failure to maintain an accurate shareholder register can invalidate share-affecting AGM resolutions; failure to report to KOTRA removes the foreign-invested enterprise status shield.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 to USD 2,500 per annum for a domestic registered agent/corporate secretarial retainer; the local registered office itself is required but does not carry a separate government renewal charge.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 to USD 20,000 per annum for a non-listed Chusik Hoesa with cross-border anti-dumping trade defense consulting revenue; the fee increases with revenue volume, related-party transactions and mandatory K-IFRS conversion.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax for taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion; plus 10% local income tax surtax resulting in a 26.4% combined top marginal rate. Lower marginal brackets are 9%, 19%, and 21%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korea does not maintain a general statutory tax holiday. Preferential deductions and exemptions are available under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act for venture and SME corporations, including 50% to 100% income tax exemptions for certified venture enterprises, R&D and software competitiveness tax credits of 25% to 50%, foreign investment cash grants, and employment creation tax deductions. For ISIC 7490 trade-defense consulting services, meaningful relief generally requires qualifying R&D or venture certification.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Return, NTS Form No. 49, filed exclusively through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal (www.hometax.go.kr). Mandatory e-filing applies to all business corporations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return with a semi-annual interim prepayment return for corporations that had prior-year taxable income. No quarterly or monthly corporate income tax returns are required.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return must be filed within three months after the fiscal year-end, so March 31 for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa. An extension of up to one month may be granted by the NTS upon application; audited conglomerate or consolidated filers have statutory administrative extensions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business registration number, legal entity name, head office address, representative director, main business code, and fiscal-year period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Chusik Hoesa with non-resident shareholders, record the foreign-invested enterprise registration number and attach the foreign investment report; do not treat the Korean entity as a branch or permanent establishment of the shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year opening and closing dates, filing status indicator, tax office jurisdiction, and industry classification code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the statutory fiscal year registered with the NTS and the ISIC 7490 or equivalent business code; report all domestic-source anti-dumping defense service revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book net income per the audited income statement prepared under K-IFRS or K-GAAP, including revenue and expense recognition, accruals, and inventory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile all consulting fees from anti-dumping defense services into Korean-source income; convert foreign-currency amounts at the Bank of Korea basic exchange rate prevailing on the transaction or fiscal-year-end date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expense adjustments, including entertainment, fines, penalties, political contributions, and expenses without documented business purpose.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disallow management or service fees paid to offshore related parties lacking economic substance; obtain contemporaneous invoices, contracts, and evidence of actual service delivery.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-exempt income and statutory income deductions, including venture/SME exemptions and Restriction of Special Taxation Act deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Entity-level tax incentives may reduce the Korean entity's tax; shareholder-level non-resident taxes are not aggregated or reported on the entity return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carryforward deduction from prior fiscal years, subject to the 10-year carryforward limit and continuity of ownership requirements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the loss carryforward schedule and reconcile prior returns; non-resident ownership changes may restrict the loss carryforward under the ownership continuity rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross corporate income tax computed by applying the progressive 9%, 19%, 21%, and 24% brackets to the taxable income base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the statutory tax before credits using the national rate only; the local income tax surtax is added separately at the surtax stage.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits including foreign tax credits, R&D tax credits, employment credits, temporary investment credits, and minimum tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim credits only at the Korean entity level; direct foreign tax credits must be supported by foreign return and tax payment certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local income tax surtax equal to 10% of the national corporate income tax computed on Line 5a after statutory credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the entity's own annual filing, compute the 10% local surtax separately; do not confuse this with the 2% local component already withheld from non-resident shareholder dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of interim prepayment taxes, prior credits, and withheld amounts, producing the final net corporate tax payable or refund due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If treaty rate relief on dividends or royalties is claimed, attach the relevant treaty exemption application and Tax Residency Certificate; any overwithholding is recovered through an amended return or refund claim within the statutory period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file by the statutory deadline attracts an unpaid-tax penalty of 20% of the tax due; underreporting penalties are 10% of the omitted tax unless the understatement is fraudulent, in which case the penalty is 20% to 30%. A daily late-payment surcharge of 0.022% per day, approximately 8.03% per annum, accrues on unpaid corporate tax. Additional fines apply for failure to attach mandatory schedules, for electronic filing violations, and for false or altered tax invoices.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% statutory dividend withholding tax on gross distributions to non-resident individual and corporate shareholders, composed of 20% national income tax plus 2% local income tax surtax, unless reduced under an applicable DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The withholding agent or the non-resident shareholder must submit to the National Tax Service a treaty reduction/exemption application through HomeTax before the payment remittance, attaching: a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority, a declaration of beneficial ownership, evidence of the shareholding period, and the applicable DTA provision. Upon NTS approval, the reduced treaty rate is applied at source. If tax is overwithheld, the non-resident shareholder may file a domestic refund claim or invoke the Mutual Agreement Procedure under the treaty; documentary support must include the original beneficial owner certificate and confirmation from the treaty counterpart tax office.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest and IP royalties paid to non-residents are each subject to a statutory withholding rate of 22% (20% national plus 2% local surtax). Under most Korean DTAs, interest rates are reduced to 10% or 15%; royalty rates are typically reduced to 10% or 15%, with certain industrial and commercial royalty categories reduced to 5% under selected treaties. Professional consulting fees that are not embedded in royalties are generally treated as business profits and are taxable in Korea only when attributable to a domestic permanent establishment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File documentation is mandatory when cross-border transactions with foreign related parties in a fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 5 billion. Master File documentation is required when the Korean entity belongs to an international business group with consolidated group revenue of at least KRW 100 billion and international related-party transactions exceeding KRW 10 billion. Country-by-Country Report filing is triggered at the same KRW 100 billion consolidated group revenue threshold, subject to the filing and notification requirements under Korea's Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea has no separate standalone Economic Substance Regulations analogous to the UAE ESR, but the Korean tax authorities and courts apply a robust substance-over-form doctrine, the general anti-abuse rule, the business-purpose doctrine, and the principal-purpose test under DTAs. A Chusik Hoesa engaged in ISIC 7490 anti-dumping trade-defense consulting must maintain real employees, physical premises, board minutes, contracts, invoices, bank accounts, commercial risk-bearing, and actual decision-making functions. A shell entity with no substantive economic activity will be disregarded, recharacterized, or treated as a conduit, and treaty benefits and transfer pricing positions will be denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Tax Evasion and False Reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting anti-dumping defense consulting revenues, registering fictitious invoices, fabricating expense deductions, destroying accounting records, or submitting materially false corporate income tax returns to the NTS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Immediate assessment of the deficient corporate tax plus dishonesty penalties of 30% to 40%, underreporting penalties of 10% to 20%, and a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.022%. Criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act carries imprisonment of up to five years and fines of up to three times the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and representatives may face personal criminal imprisonment, personal monetary fines, civil restitution orders, travel bans under the National Tax Collection Act, and secondary collection against personal assets for taxes withheld from employees or suppliers and not remitted.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse and Sham Transaction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a paper Chusik Hoesa with no employees, office, payroll, operational records, or economic activity; routing anti-dumping defense fees through the shell to foreign equity holders; creating corresponding artificial deductibility without actual service performance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard or recharacterization of the entity and its transactions, denial of DTA benefits, disallowance of all related deductions, add-back of expenses to the taxable base, imposition of 20% to 40% unfaithful-return penalties, and an order to cease the illegal trade practice in egregious cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil where the company is a mere instrumentality; directors and beneficial owners are jointly liable for the unpaid corporate tax, are subject to departure restraint, and face criminal sanction if the sham was used to evade taxes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Price Manipulation and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length fees to foreign related parties for cross-border anti-dumping consulting services, failing to prepare or file the Local File and Master File at the KRW thresholds, or using fabricated benchmarks to support unrealistic royalty or service margins.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS will make an arm's-length price adjustment, apply secondary adjustments, impose a 10% to 20% transfer pricing penalty, and add daily late-payment surcharges. Failure to file mandatory documentation triggers additional fixed penalties and may deprive the taxpayer of the statutory burden-of-proof benefit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or direct false TP documentation are personally liable for civil damages to the company and to the tax authority, jointly responsible for penalties where gross negligence or willfulness is shown, and subject to criminal prosecution and travel bans in aggravated cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Disguised Profit Repatriation and Dividend Withholding Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Reclassifying dividends as tax-deductible consulting, management, licensing, or interest payments to foreign shareholders; distributing profits without withholding the 22% statutory dividend tax; using circular loans or offshore intermediary entities to disguise repatriation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payment is recharacterized as a dividend; the net taxable income is increased through disallowance of the disguised expense; the 22% withholding tax is collected from the distributing entity together with a 20% unreported penalty, daily 0.022% late-payment surcharges, and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the uncollected withholding tax as statutory withholding agents; civil restitution may be imposed; criminal penalties of imprisonment up to three years or fines apply, and the NTS may issue travel bans and freeze director and shareholder assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Unlicensed Trade Defense Activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting Swift wire or wire-transfer payments from undisclosed third-party beneficial owners without conducting customer due diligence, structuring fee payments to evade KRW transaction reporting thresholds, or providing anti-dumping defense representation without the statutory license and registration required for trade-remedy legal practice.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations of the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information carry imprisonment of up to three years or fines up to KRW 30 million, plus confiscation of proceeds. Unlicensed practice of trade defense law triggers administrative suspension, revocation of licenses, and separate fines under the relevant legal-services regulation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally responsible for AML compliance and licensing supervision; they may be personally fined, criminally detained, banned from leaving Korea, and held civilly liable for losses sustained by clients or the tax authority in connection with unreported suspicious wire transfers.
